# Intake Brief — Update the README description of the game

## Headline

Correct the README's opening description so Main Street is presented as an
**economic city builder** in which the player develops the **commercial hub of
a city**, not as a shop-management / small-business game.

## Problem statement

The README's lead paragraph currently describes Main Street as "a small-business
engine-builder played card by card on a shared high street", which frames the
game as shop management. That framing is wrong: Main Street is an **economic
city builder** where the player seeks to develop the commercial hub of a city.
The inaccurate first impression misleads prospective players and contributors
landing on the repository.

## Users

- **Prospective players** landing on the GitHub repository or the published web
  build, who decide whether the game is for them from the README opener.
  - *As a prospective player, I want the README's first description of the game
    to state its true genre so I know immediately whether it is the kind of game
    I want to play.*
- **Contributors and maintainers** who rely on the README as the canonical
  high-level description of the project.
  - *As a contributor, I want the project's top-level description to match the
    actual game design so I can orient myself correctly.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The README's opening description no longer characterises Main Street as a
  shop-management / small-business game.
- [ ] The opening description presents Main Street as an **economic city
  builder** in which the player develops the **commercial hub of a city**,
  consistent with the game design in
  `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §1 (town planner revitalising
  a street grid).
- [ ] The revised opener retains the accurate framing that this repository is a
  single-game distribution of the Tableau Card Engine — one playable example
  game (Main Street) plus the core-owned Gym.
- [ ] Validation: an automated docs check (or a focused unit test asserting on
  README content) confirms the stale "small-business / shop management" framing
  is absent and the corrected "economic city builder"/"commercial hub" framing
  is present in `README.md`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only change; no gameplay or runtime code behaviour changes.
- Must keep the canonical terminology from
  `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §1.1 (turn = week; avoid
  "day"/"today" synonyms). The terminology guard lives at
  `core/scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.
- Keep the existing README structure (title, launcher description, published
  URL); only the genre description is corrected.
- Prefer a minimal, surgical wording change rather than a README rewrite.

## Existing state

- `README.md` lines 3–7: "Main Street is a single-game distribution of the
  Tableau Card Engine: a small-business engine-builder played card by card on a
  shared high street. This repository builds a launcher that contains exactly
  one playable example game — **Main Street** — alongside the core-owned
  **Gym** ...".
- No other repo file uses the "small-business engine-builder" phrasing; the
  genre mismatch is confined to this README opener.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §1 defines the game as a
  single-player, turn-based tableau card game where the player is a town
  planner revitalising a street grid.
- Tests follow a docs-drift pattern (`tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/investor-docs.test.ts`) that assert documented content,
  which is the natural home for the validation criterion.

## Desired change

Rewrite the README's opening description to describe Main Street as an economic
city builder in which the player develops the commercial hub of a city, while
preserving the "single-game distribution of the Tableau Card Engine" framing and
the launcher/existing-example-game explanation. Add a focused docs test asserting
the corrected description.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `README.md` — Replace the "small-business engine-builder" genre framing in the
  opening paragraph with the economic-city-builder / commercial-hub description.
- `tests/main-street/README-description.test.ts` (new) — Assert the README opener
  presents the correct genre and omits the stale framing.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Reference only (canonical
  description to align with); change only if it also carries the stale framing.

## Related work

- **Potentially related docs**
  - `README.md` — the file being corrected.
  - `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — canonical game overview
    (§1) defining the game's actual design; source of truth for the corrected
    description.
  - `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md` — historical GDD; player is a town
    planner revitalising a street grid.
  - `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`,
    `tests/main-street/investor-docs.test.ts` — existing docs-drift test
    patterns to follow.
- **Potentially related work items**
  - `Update documentation for Investor card and mechanics (MS-0MUOSUMNK000QZ62)`
    — completed docs update, same doc-drift approach.
  - `Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift guard
    (MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY)` — completed docs tooling/guard work.
  - `Fix stale example-games/main-street paths in docs after the src/ migration
    (MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5)` — open docs-accuracy item in the same documentation
    area (not a duplicate; different content).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV1HALJ20003VK6** – [test-failure] expanded-viewport.browser.test.ts > places a held card on the shared four-way corner through the camera transform (AC1/AC2) — failing test (completed)
- **MS-0MV33TDGV00433IA** – Test: per-seat Game Over challenge breakdown (completed)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** ambiguous genre wording could over-claim (e.g. implying a full 3D

  a card-based economic builder where the player develops a commercial hub.
- **Risk (scope creep):** reorganising or rewriting more of the README than the

  documentation gaps as separate work items.
- **Assumption:** the README opening paragraph is the "description" referred to
  by the work item; no GitHub repository-description metadata is in scope.
- **Assumption:** documentation-only change, so no build/runtime risk beyond the

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the seed context (the work-item
description) fully specified the problem, the correct genre, and the target
file, and repo search confirmed the mismatch is confined to the README opener.

- Q: *(none asked)* — Intake skipped the interview because the seed context was

# Intake Brief — Spread tier reputation thresholds and cap tier unlocks to one per game

Work item: **MS-0MV88T4I6000HQZG** — "Spread tier reputation thresholds per Monte Carlo ranges and cap tier unlocks to one per game" (`feature`, priority `high`)

## Headline

Tier unlocks by reputation currently fire in bursts (a median Medium run clears the 400/800/1200/1600 rungs in one go), so the ladder reveals content without pacing. Re-derive the 12-tier reputation thresholds from the Monte-Carlo-measured reputation distribution (Medium, achievement-rate steps) and cap progression at **one tier unlock per run**.

## Problem statement

Reputation thresholds for the early tiers (T2–T5 = 400/800/1200/1600) sit far below typical end-of-run reputation: a median Medium run ends around 2,900 rep, so `updateCampaignAfterRun` unlocks **4–6 tiers in a single run** (400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400 are all cleared, adding the challenge triggers). Multiple new card families appear at once, there is no sense of a hard-won milestone, and the remaining ladder (up to T12 = 8000) is far out of reach — an unsatisfying pacing cliff at both ends.

## Users

Main Street players engaging with the campaign meta-progression (unlock ladder). The reputation path is the primary unlock driver; the challenge path is an alternative trigger per PRD M2.

Example user stories:
- "As a returning player, I want each run to unlock at most one new tier so that unlocking a tier feels like a milestone rather than a content dump."
- "As a player climbing the ladder, I want thresholds spaced so that consecutive unlocks are genuinely earned across several runs."
- "As a challenge-focused player, I still want the challenge path to unlock tiers, but it must obey the same one-per-run pacing."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Threshold spread (reputation path).** The 12-tier reputation thresholds are re-derived from a **fresh Medium Monte-Carlo run on current HEAD** (≥ 200 seeds, greedy strategy via `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts`, `economyHistory` final reputation) to hit the target achievement shares — the % of Medium runs whose end-of-run reputation clears the tier: **T2 90%, T3 75%, T4 60%, T5 45%, T6 35%, T7 25%, T8 18%, T9 12%, T10 8%, T11 4%, T12 1%**. The derived thresholds are recorded with the MC evidence (percentile table, run counts). Exact values may be rounded to friendly numbers and document that rounding; monotonic increasing order is preserved. (Existing `results/level2-gate-before-*.json` are treated as stale — generated 2026-10-07, before later balance changes; a fresh run is required.)
2. **T12 / top tiers stay aspirational.** No threshold is artificially compressed into the observed rep range; T12 (and the top tiers) may sit above the observed maximum and remain primarily challenge-path / long-campaign reachable.
3. **One tier unlock per run.** `updateCampaignAfterRun` (in `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`) unlocks **at most one** tier per completed run: the **lowest newly-eligible locked tier** (no skipping), regardless of whether eligibility came from the reputation path, the challenge path, or both.
4. **Challenge path preserved but capped.** All challenge-based unlock conditions remain unchanged and still work as an alternative trigger; the one-per-run cap applies to them identically.
5. **UI consistency.** Any surface showing a tier threshold or next-tier target (e.g. `findNextLockedTier`/`scoreNextTierLabel` in `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`) reflects the new thresholds; no stale hard-coded figures remain in i18n/UI text.
6. **Tests.** `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` is updated: the existing "unlocks multiple tiers in a single high-reputation run" case becomes an assertion that exactly one (lowest) tier unlocks; new cases cover cap semantics (rep-only, challenge-only, both-triggers, next-run continuation, already-unlocked tiers, T12 aspirational). All existing tier/progression/save-load tests continue to pass.
7. **Evidence + docs.** The Monte-Carlo reputation-distribution evidence and the new threshold table are committed, and the relevant docs are updated: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (US-1/update notes + threshold calibration appendix), plus `content-design-and-progression.md` if it restates thresholds. CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (ship skill manages it).
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the change (unit + unit-cli + smoke, per the test skill).

## Constraints

- **Calibration basis (Q2-A):** thresholds are calibrated on **Medium** difficulty only. Easy runs will generally unlock faster and Hard runs slower — accepted drift documented in the brief/PRD (one ladder cannot pace all three economies equally).
- **No skipping (Q1-A):** the one-per-run cap always unlocks the **lowest** newly-eligible locked tier; the ladder is never jumped.
- **Achievement-rate steps (Q3-B):** thresholds are not evenly spaced; they are placed to hit the pre-defined share steps above. Where the Medium distribution is clumpy (a 5% band between ~794 and ~2152 yields a large threshold gap; the ≥2000–4500 mass yields tight mid-ladder gaps), the shares are authoritative and thresholds follow the data.
- **Challenge conditions unchanged** — out of scope to redesign; only their interaction with the cap changes.
- `campaign.unlockedTiers` / `milestoneHistory` schema and save/load format unchanged (only the number of tiers appended per run changes).

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetTiers.ts` — `TIER_CONFIG` holds the 12 thresholds: 0, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400, 3200, 4000, 4800, 5600, 6400, 8000; card-to-tier mapping lives in `src/card-data.csv` (out of scope here).
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` `updateCampaignAfterRun` — iterates all locked tiers; `if (reputationMet || challengeMet) campaign.unlockedTiers.push(...)` → multi-unlock per run.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `findNextLockedTier` shows `requires Rep ≥ <threshold>`.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — US-1 tests pin old thresholds (400→T2, etc.) and explicitly pin "unlocks multiple tiers in a single high-reputation run".
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` §2/§8 (US-1) and Appendix B — PRD originally specified multi-tier unlock and 5-tier thresholds; expanded to 12 tiers (CG-0MT3C744B009DS84).
- Existing MC evidence: `results/level2-gate-before-greedy-{easy,medium,hard}.json` (200 runs each, 2026-10-07). Medium: mean 2632, median 2896, p10 132, p25 794, p50 2900, p75 3752, p90 4712, max 6272.
- MC harness records per-turn `economyHistory` (incl. reputation) but **not** `challengesCompleted` per run — challenge-path shares are measured separately or estimated during implementation; the share table above is reputation-path.

## Desired change

1. Run a fresh Medium MC calibration pass on HEAD; extract the final-reputation distribution.
2. Compute thresholds from the share table (percentile lookup), round sensibly, keep monotonic.
3. Update `TIER_CONFIG` thresholds.
4. Add the one-per-run cap (lowest eligible) to `updateCampaignAfterRun`.
5. Update the HUD-tier tooltip plumbing only if the new thresholds flow through configuration (no hard-coded UI strings).
6. Update tests + PRD/evidence docs.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetTiers.ts` — `TIER_CONFIG.reputationThreshold` values (primary change).
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — `updateCampaignAfterRun` one-per-run cap (primary change).
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` / `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — fresh calibration evidence; note the harness currently omits per-run `challengesCompleted` (add if needed for challenge-path evidence).
- `results/main-street-monte-carlo*.json` — committed calibration evidence artifacts.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — cap + threshold tests.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — verify next-tier threshold display uses `TIER_DEFINITIONS` (update if any stale constants remain).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — US-1/update notes, threshold calibration appendix.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — threshold restatements if any.
- `docs/dev/` / `CHANGELOG.md` — CHANGELOG excluded; no docs/dev change expected.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Clumpy MC distribution:** the Medium rep distribution is bimodal (a low cluster ~0–800 that includes collapsed/bankrupt runs and a dense 2000–4500 body). Percentile-derived mid-ladder thresholds will be close together (hundreds apart) on the dense body; the one-per-run cap is what prevents burst unlocks there, and the share steps are authoritative — exact value selection must be documented so the "too close together" complaint does not silently return.
- **Stale calibration source:** existing `results/` MC files predate later balance changes; thresholds are only finalised against a fresh run on HEAD. If the fresh distribution differs materially, the share table survives and threshold *values* follow the new percentiles (replan, do not fudge).
- **Challenge-path shares unknown:** the MC harness does not record per-run `challengesCompleted`; the share table above is reputation-path only. Adding challenge-path evidence is a possible small harness scope increase (note in plan, do not silently expand).
- **Save/load & schema:** only the number of tiers appended per run changes; `milestoneHistory` entries remain per-unlock (one per qualifying run). Existing saves with already-unlocked tiers must not regress (multi-tier saves keep their tiers).
- **UI text:** thresholds appear in HUD tooltip text — any hard-coded numbers must flow from `TIER_DEFINITIONS`; flag dead constants rather than silently updating strings in isolation.
- **Scope-creep guard:** redesigning challenge conditions, rebalancing rep sources, or adjusting card-to-tier assignments are explicitly out of scope; record such opportunities as linked work items, not gold-plating here.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** (completed, high) — "Re-tune reputation sources…": ×4 retune of rep sources directly inflates the rep scale and makes the pre-retune thresholds (and any pre-retune calibration) stale.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** (completed) — Level-2 gate MC evidence (`results/level2-gate-*.json`): source of the current (stale) reputation distribution.
- **MS-0MUQUBK1B006EODZ / MS-0MUQUBJ4J000IQT7** (completed) — Monte-Carlo baseline and evidence methodology this calibration extends.
- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** (completed) — 5-turn payback rebalance; relevant economy vector.
- **MS-0MUYGFVIJ00070MB** (completed) — Reputation-phase invariant regression tests (guard against rep-path regressions while touching thresholds).
- Docs: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (M2 tier ladder, US-1, Appendix B), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `docs/main-street/reputation-retune-evidence.md`.

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers (interview round)

# Engine: per-owner piggyback rewards and join-fully cost (F2)

## Target outcome
Engine helpers that (a) compute an eligible event's rewards on the piggybacker's OWN board at a 1.0 (join fully) / 0.5 (free-ride) scale, and (b) apply the join-fully cost — exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid — to the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, spending no action point.

## Context
- Rewards reuse the existing per-owner event math inside `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (SpecificSynergy counts the owner's own matching businesses; reputation multiplier per owner; staff mitigation per owner).
- Cost baseline is the amount the acting player actually paid at play time (after any discounts the acting player holds), not the nominal CSV cost.
- Competitive authority: mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`; never the shared `resourceBank` (replay and save/deserialize untouched).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** A shared, non-mutating projection computes an owner-specific event reward at a scale factor (0.5 / 1.0) using the owner's own boards, including per-owner reputation multipliers and staff mitigation.
- [ ] **AC2** Join-fully deducts exactly `round(1.5 * paidCost)` from the piggybacker's coins, never a partial charge; `actionBudget` / `actionsRemaining` are unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3** Unaffordable join-fully is a no-op (option unavailable, nothing charged); the 50% free-ride is applied in that case by the caller.
- [ ] **AC4** Unit tests assert exact before/after coin and reputation values for both tiers on a piggybacker board with and without matching businesses, plus an unchanged action budget.

- [ ] **Satisfies epic AC2** — - [ ] **AC2 — Join-fully tier.** Choosing "join fully" deducts exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event from the piggybacker's own coin balance (and **no action point**), then credits the piggybacker 100% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board). The option is unavailable (and never partially charged) when the piggybacker cannot afford the cost. Verified by unit tests asserting exact before/after coin and reputation values and an unchanged action budget.
- [ ] **Satisfies epic AC3** — - [ ] **AC3 — Free-ride tier.** Every non-acting eligible player automatically receives 50% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board) with no prompt to decline, spending no action point and no coins. This is also the fallback when "join fully" is unaffordable. Verified by unit tests.

## Minimal implementation
- Extract/reuse the per-owner delta computation from `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` into a scale-aware read-only projection and a mutating apply helper for a given seat.
- Capture `paidCost` at event play time (see F3) and implement the 150% rule in the apply helper.
- Unit tests in a new `tests/main-street/piggyback-engine-rewards.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts
- src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts
- tests/main-street/piggyback-engine-rewards.test.ts (new)

## Dependencies
- F1 (eligibility flag).

## Deliverables
Scale-aware reward projection + join-fully cost application + unit tests.

# Pending piggyback decision state machine (F3)

## Target outcome
When a piggybackable Investment event is played in competitive mode (N≥2), raise one pending decision per other ACTIVE seat, pause the shared day after the acting player's resolution completes, and resolve each seat in seat order (join fully or automatic 50% free-ride) with full determinism and persistence, reusing the `pendingEventChoice` pause/resume pattern.

## Context
- Only non-eliminated seats get decisions (see MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2).
- Decisions resolve one seat at a time, independently, in seat order (intake Q4). No additional RNG draws in the resolution path (AC4 determinism).
- Free-ride is automatic; the only choice is the join-fully upgrade (F5 UI, F4 AI).
- N=1 and non-eligible events produce no pending state and no pause.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** Playing an eligible event via any dispatch path (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`, `playHeldEvent`) in N≥2 raises pending piggyback decisions for every other active seat and surfaces a pause (e.g. `TurnResult` flag + `state.pendingPiggyback*`) after the acting player's effects resolve; N=1 and non-eligible events never pause.
- [ ] **AC2** `resolvePendingPiggyback` applies the 50% free-ride automatically per seat and the join-fully upgrade (F2) when chosen and affordable; seats resolve independently in seat order.
- [ ] **AC3** Acting player's reward and all shared decks (market/incident) are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback resolutions; replay equality test proves zero extra RNG draws.
- [ ] **AC4** Pending decisions serialize/deserialize (null default for older saves); serialize→deserialize→resolve completes the day without stalling.
- [ ] **AC5** Eliminated seats are skipped; a human-vs-AI and an N>2 test both cover the ordering.

- [ ] **Satisfies epic AC4** — - [ ] **AC4 — Isolation, determinism & persistence.** The acting player's reward and all shared decks are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback decisions; decisions for N>2 are resolved independently per seat in a deterministic order with no additional RNG draws; a pending piggyback decision survives a save/load round-trip. Verified by tests (including a replay/equality check and a serialize→deserialize→resolve test).

## Minimal implementation
- Add `pendingPiggyback` state shape (per-seat entries: seatId, event, paidCost, chosenJoin, resolved) to `MainStreetStateTypes.ts` and a pause flag to `EngineTypes` (`TurnResult`).
- Raise the decision from the event-play dispatch paths in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (after `applyCompetitiveEventEffects`).
- Add the resolve function and integrate with `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` (headless auto-resolve so the Monte Carlo loop never stalls — mirrors `resolveCompetitivePendingChoice`).
- Serialize/deserialize in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` + `MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`.
- Tests: state machine, determinism/replay, save/load, N>2 order, elimination.

## Key Files
- src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts
- src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts
- src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts
- src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts
- src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts
- src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts
- src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts
- tests/main-street/piggyback-state-machine.test.ts, tests/main-street/piggyback-save-load.test.ts (new)

## Dependencies
- F1 (flag), F2 (reward/cost helpers).

## Deliverables
Pending-decision state machine, pause/resume, persistence, determinism and N>2 tests.

# Deterministic AI piggyback join-fully policy (F4)

## Target outcome
AI seats decide join-fully vs keep-50% via a deterministic, non-RNG heuristic that shares one affordability predicate with the eligibility gate, so headless and Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible and legal.

## Context
- Applies when the AI is a piggybacker (another seat organised an eligible event).
- The AI must never attempt join-fully without the coins (risk: AI legality).
- Policy heuristic (proposal): join fully when the event's projected own-board reward (×1.0) exceeds the 150% cost AND the remaining balance stays above a difficulty-visible floor; otherwise keep the free-ride. Exact shape is implementation detail; must be deterministic and difficulty-aware.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** `decidePiggyback(...)` (engine/AI) returns 'join' | 'free-ride' deterministically with no RNG; identical inputs → identical outputs.
- [ ] **AC2** The shared affordability predicate gates both the eligibility check and the AI policy; the AI never joins when unaffordable.
- [ ] **AC3** The headless competitive/AI day loop auto-resolves pending piggyback decisions so the sim never stalls (`driveAiSeatsUntilClosing` / Monte Carlo harness).
- [ ] **AC4** Unit tests cover affordability edges, heuristic thresholds, and a replay determinism check; the competitive Monte Carlo harness exercises the AI path.

- [ ] **Satisfies epic AC5** — - [ ] **AC5 — AI policy and human prompt.** AI seats decide whether to join fully via a deterministic strategy heuristic in `MainStreetAiStrategy`; the human seat is offered the choice to join fully (pay the cost for 100%) or keep the automatic 50% free-ride, through the existing choice/prompt plumbing. Verified by an AI-policy unit test and a scene/command-layer test for the human prompt.

## Minimal implementation
- Add the decision function (next to `decideEventChoice` in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` or in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`), plus the shared affordability predicate.

Deterministic AI join-fully policy + shared affordability predicate + tests.

# Full-suite verification and competitive balance check (F7)

## Target outcome
The complete project test suite passes with the piggyback mechanic and the competitive Monte Carlo harness shows no unmitigated economy runaway from 100%-reward piggyback participation (risk mitigation).

## Context
- Economy-runaway risk (intake): stacking 100% rewards across organiser events could inflate a seat's economy; the 150% premium is the primary mitigation — measure before/after.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill (/skill:test); failures are triaged via the triage skill into `test-failure` work items.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** Full test suite passes with the new changes (unit + smoke scope, run via the test skill).
- [ ] **AC2** Competitive Monte Carlo run recorded before/after the mechanic (win-rate / score attribution); any drift beyond noise is documented in a comment on the epic with a recommendation. Snapshots are regenerated only when the shift is an intended balance change (see `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` policy).
- [ ] **AC3** New piggyback tests (F1–F5) are present and green.

- [ ] **Satisfies epic AC7** — - [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTIIL1ON006H7IL** – Shared-day phase machine: alternating MarketPhases, shared closing phases (completed)
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – When playing with AI player is credit with AI challenges (open)
- **MS-0MUQZH6BU002113D** – GitHub Pages deploy workflow (completed)

### Repository file matches

# CSV option encoding and compilation

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Replace the three legacy CSV columns with a single `options` column and compile
it into the generalised `StorylineOption` list carrying candidate successor
sets.

## Scope

Deliver the authoring-to-compilation half of the vertical slice (CSV → compiled
model); runtime resolution lands in F3.

## CSV encoding (decided in planning)

- Column: `options`, replacing `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`.
- Encoding: `label|cardA,cardB;label2|cardC`
  - `;` separates options, `|` separates label from candidates, `,` separates candidate card ids.
  - Blank / absent ⇒ non-choice node (no options).
  - `label|` (empty candidate list) ⇒ terminal option: the chain ends.
- Options are always `apply` (producer Q4=B); `skip` remains available only via
  the programmatic `registerStorylineOptions` seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A storyline choice node can declare an arbitrary number of labelled options authored via CSV in `src/card-data.csv`, each option carrying an ordered candidate list of successor card ids, where an empty list ends the chain.
- The two-way `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` fields are removed from the CSV header and the compiled Accept/Reject semantics are replaced by the arbitrary-outcome model, with no backward compatibility retained.
- `StorylineOption` exposes the option's candidate successor ids; CSV compilation always emits `effectPolicy: 'apply'` and derives `hasChoices` from a non-empty option list.
- The encoding is parsed deterministically with whitespace trimmed, and an encoding that is non-empty but decodes to no valid option is rejected rather than silently ignored.
- One tracer storyline row (e.g. `evt-recession`) is migrated end-to-end and resolves through the new compiled model.
- The CSV column reference documentation in `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` documents the new encoding.

## Notes

- `event.hasChoices` is retained as the derived predicate; a node has choices
  iff its decoded option list is non-empty.

**Key Files:**

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `options` column; legacy columns removed.

# Engine resolution and option tokens

Part of **MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144** — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Goal

Make runtime resolution draw the successor uniformly at random from the chosen
option's candidate set and carry the chosen option through transcript/save/undo
as a stable token.

## Scope

Runtime half of the vertical slice: `resolveStorylineOption`, pending-choice
lifecycle, transcript token, save/undo round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When an option is chosen, exactly one successor is drawn uniformly at random from that option's candidate set using the seeded `state.rng()` (one draw per selection, at resolution time), so replaying with the same seed produces the same successor and the option list the player sees is unchanged by the draw.
- Resolution precedence is: `successorResolver` callback (if present) over the random draw over an empty/absent candidate list ending the chain; `effectPolicy` is still honoured for registry-authored options.
- Transcript records the chosen option as a label token; the legacy `'accept'`/`'reject'` tokens are removed and no legacy-save migration is implemented (producer Q5: no saves in the wild).
- `pendingEventChoice` save/undo round-trips an arbitrary option list without loss, preserving the chosen token, and `resolveEventChoice` indexing works over any option count.
- Unit tests in `tests/main-street/MainStreetEngineEventChoice.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/MainStreetEventChoiceUndo.test.ts` pass.

## Notes

- The draw must be exactly one `state.rng()` call per selection; any additional
  draw shifts the seeded stream and must be pinned by tests.

# AI staff should not give players bonus hand slots

## Problem Statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, a staff card's hand-capacity bonus
(`handSlotsAdded`) leaks across seats: when an AI seat hires a staff card that
grants an extra hand slot, the human player also gains a slot, and vice versa.
Only the seat that employs the staff should receive its bonuses.

## Users

- **Competitive human player** — expects their hand capacity to depend only on
  the staff *they* employ.
- **AI seat (opponent)** — should get hand capacity only from its own staff.
- **Developer / QA** — needs deterministic, per-seat hand capacity that survives
  seat switching and save/load.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, when my AI opponent hires a staff member that adds a
  hand slot, my own hand capacity must not change.
- As a competitive player, when I hire a staff member that adds a hand slot,
  only my hand capacity must increase.
- As a developer, per-seat hand capacity must round-trip through
  `bindCompetitiveSeat`/`restoreCompetitiveSeat` and through save/load.

## Root Cause (from code inspection)

- `MainStreetState.maxHandSize` is a single shared scalar
  (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts:440`).
- `purchaseStaffCard` mutates the shared scalar:
  `state.maxHandSize += card.handSlotsAdded`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:912`); `layoffStaffCard` decrements it
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:675`).
- Competitive seat switching copies `coins`, `reputation`, `hand`,
  `staffCards` and `actionBudget` between the shared fields and the acting
  `PlayerRecord`, but **not** `maxHandSize`
  (`bindCompetitiveSeat` / `restoreCompetitiveSeat`,
  `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:2595`/`2608`). `PlayerRecord`
  (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts:226`) has no `maxHandSize` field.
- Consequently the shared scalar is neither saved nor restored per seat: a
  bonus earned by one seat inflates every other seat's hand capacity, and the
  last-seat value persists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Hiring a staff card with `handSlotsAdded > 0` by one competitive seat
   increases **only that seat's** hand capacity; every other seat's capacity is
   unchanged. Verified by a unit test that binds each seat, hires the staff, and
   asserts each seat's capacity.
2. Laying off / losing a staff card decreases **only the employing seat's**
   hand capacity (respecting the existing minimum, currently 2).
3. `bindCompetitiveSeat` then `restoreCompetitiveSeat` round-trips hand
   capacity per seat, so alternating seats each observe their own capacity.
4. Per-seat hand capacity persists through save/load; legacy saves without a
   per-seat value default to the base capacity (3 where appropriate) and
   preserved grown values are not reset.
5. Single-player behaviour is unchanged (base 3 plus staff `handSlotsAdded`).
6. Existing hand-capacity, competitive, and staff unit/browser tests pass.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep `state.maxHandSize` as the shared working field bound per seat, matching
  the existing competitive binding pattern for coins/hand/staff/action budget;
  do not restructure the binding model.
- Do not change card-data `handSlotsAdded` values.
- Saves must remain backward compatible (legacy saves load unchanged).

## Existing State

- `maxHandSize` starts at 3 (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:659`,
  `TutorialScenario.ts:399`) and is growable without a hard cap via staff
  `handSlotsAdded` (`docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:172`).
- `PlayerRecord` carries per-seat `coins`, `reputation`, `hand`, `staffCards`,
  `actionBudget`, `score`, controller/strategy/difficulty, colour and
  `eliminated` — but no hand capacity.
- Competitive state is created in `createCompetitiveState`
  (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:791`).
- Saves serialise `players` wholesale
  (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts:103`) with a seat-config backfill on load.
- Two competitive seats are known to hire staff through `GreedyStrategy`, which
  enumerates `hire-staff` actions (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:818`).

## Desired Change

- Add a per-seat hand-capacity field (e.g. `maxHandSize`) to `PlayerRecord`.
- Initialise it to the base capacity (3) in `createCompetitiveState`.
- Bind it in `bindCompetitiveSeat` and write it back in
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat`, so `purchaseStaffCard` / `layoffStaffCard` operate on
  the acting seat's value.
- Persist the per-seat value through save/load, defaulting legacy saves without
  the field to the base capacity (preserving grown values).
- Leave single-player paths unchanged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add `maxHandSize` to `PlayerRecord`.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — bind/restore the per-seat hand capacity.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — initialise the per-seat field in
  `createCompetitiveState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise/backfill the per-seat value.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — confirm `purchaseStaffCard` targets the
  bound (acting-seat) capacity.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — confirm `layoffStaffCard` targets the bound
  capacity.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-*.test.ts` — regression coverage for per-seat
  hand capacity.

## Related Work

- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** — Competitive state model: per-player resources,
  owner-tagged street (completed). Establishes the per-seat state model that
  hand capacity must join.
- **MS-0MUTU8JKV003UQFG** — Competitive save/load & single-player regression
  (completed). The save/load compatibility contract for per-seat state.
- **MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4** — Shared banked-actions pool semantics; documents the
  bind/restore pattern this change follows.
- **MS-0MUYAEXBN008YC0J** — Executive should grant an action point
  (in-progress). Sibling per-seat bonus investigation.
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** — Some staff cards should add action points
  (completed). Precedent for staff effects altering per-seat budgets.
- **MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1** — Reputation bonuses should have no delay between
  businesses (open). Sibling item migrated alongside this one.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** `bankedActions` is intentionally a shared pool and is out of
  scope; only hand capacity leaks per the report.
- **Risk:** other per-seat bonuses (e.g. staff-derived action budget) may share
  the same leak pattern and should be audited separately.
- **Risk:** save/load incompatibility for in-flight competitive saves; mitigated
  by a defensive default for the missing per-seat field.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any additional shared-field leaks discovered during
  implementation are recorded as new linked work items, not folded into this
  fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions were required: the problem statement is specific and
the root cause was established by code inspection (see Root Cause). No open
questions remain.

- Q (self-resolved): Which worklog is canonical for this item? — Answer:
  `MS-0MV8LHN5U008B9JJ` (tce-main-street). Evidence: migration comment on the
  Main Street item, "Migrated from OSL-0MV8L9VCW006FLB8 (open_source_llm
  worklog) on 2026-10-14", and the fact that the affected code lives in
  tce-main-street.
- Q (self-resolved): Is single-player affected? — Answer: No. Single-player has
  no seat switching, so `maxHandSize` behaves as documented. Evidence:
  `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:171-172`.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** – Competitive state model: per-player resources, owner-tagged street (completed)
- **MS-0MUYAEXBN008YC0J** – Executive should grant an action point (in-progress)
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)

- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: also, bonuses, card, extra, get (+10 more)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: also, bonuses, card, extra, get (+10 more)

# Test: per-seat hand capacity isolation in competitive play

## Summary

Test-first regression coverage for MS-0MV8LHN5U008B9JJ: verify that staff-card
hand-slot bonuses (`handSlotsAdded`) in competitive mode apply only to the seat
that employs the staff. These tests are authored first (red), define the
per-seat contract, and are made green by the sibling implementation child.

## Users / context

- **Competitive human player** — hand capacity must depend only on the staff
  they employ.
- **AI seat (opponent)** — must get hand capacity only from its own staff.
- **Developer / QA** — deterministic, per-seat hand capacity that survives seat
  switching and save/load.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A test binds each competitive seat, hires a staff card with `handSlotsAdded > 0` for one seat, and asserts only that seat's hand capacity increases while every other seat's capacity is unchanged.
2. A test lays off (or loses) a staff card and asserts only the employing seat's hand capacity decreases, respecting the existing minimum of 2.
3. A test covers the `bindCompetitiveSeat` then `restoreCompetitiveSeat` round-trip: alternating seats each observe their own capacity after bind/restore cycles.
4. A test covers per-seat persistence through save/load, including a legacy save without the per-seat field defaulting to the base capacity (3) while preserved grown values are not reset.
5. A test asserts single-player behaviour is unchanged: base 3 plus the seat's staff `handSlotsAdded`.
6. Existing hand-capacity, competitive, and staff unit/browser tests pass alongside the new regression tests, which run deterministically with the seeded RNG.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a new per-seat hand-capacity regression suite (or extend existing
  `competitive-*` suites) under `tests/main-street/`.
- Extend `competitive-save-load.test.ts` with the per-seat round-trip and a
  legacy-save-without-field case.
- Extend staff/hand tests to assert single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- Use the existing seeded-RNG helpers so every assertion is deterministic.

## Constraints

- Do not change card-data `handSlotsAdded` values.
- Tests must fail against the current shared-`maxHandSize` behaviour (red
  baseline) and pass after the fix.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first; authored before the implementation child).

## Deliverables

- Failing-first regression tests defining the per-seat hand-capacity contract.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/main-street/competitive-*.test.ts` — new per-seat hand-capacity regression coverage.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-save-load.test.ts` — save/load round-trip + legacy default.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` — single-player staff behaviour unchanged.

# Implement: per-seat hand-capacity binding and persistence

## Summary

Fix the cross-seat `handSlotsAdded` leak: give each `PlayerRecord` its own hand
capacity, bind/restore it around competitive turns, and persist it through
save/load with a legacy default, while leaving single-player behaviour
unchanged.

## Root cause (from code inspection)

- `MainStreetState.maxHandSize` is a single shared scalar
  (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts:440`).
- `purchaseStaffCard` mutates the shared scalar (`state.maxHandSize +=
  card.handSlotsAdded`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:912`);
  `layoffStaffCard` decrements it (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:675`).
- Competitive seat switching copies coins, reputation, hand, staffCards and
  actionBudget between the shared fields and the acting `PlayerRecord`, but
  **not** `maxHandSize` (`bindCompetitiveSeat` / `restoreCompetitiveSeat`,
  `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:2675/2694`). `PlayerRecord`
  (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts:226`) has no `maxHandSize` field.
- The shared scalar is therefore neither saved nor restored per seat.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `PlayerRecord` gains a per-seat `maxHandSize` field initialised to the base capacity (3) in `createCompetitiveState`.
2. `bindCompetitiveSeat` copies the acting seat's `maxHandSize` onto `state.maxHandSize` and `restoreCompetitiveSeat` writes it back.
3. Hiring a staff card with `handSlotsAdded > 0` increases only the employing seat's hand capacity; every other seat's capacity is unchanged.
4. Laying off or losing a staff card decreases only the employing seat's hand capacity, respecting the existing minimum of 2.
5. The `bindCompetitiveSeat` then `restoreCompetitiveSeat` round-trip preserves each seat's own capacity, so alternating seats each observe their own value.
6. Per-seat hand capacity persists through save/load; legacy saves without a per-seat value default to the base capacity (3) and preserved grown values are not reset.
7. Single-player behaviour is unchanged: base 3 plus staff `handSlotsAdded`, via the existing `state.maxHandSize` path.
8. Existing hand-capacity, competitive, and staff unit/browser tests pass, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `maxHandSize` to `PlayerRecord` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`).
- Initialise it to the base capacity (3) in `createCompetitiveState`
  (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:791`), matching the per-seat binding pattern
  for coins/hand/staff/actionBudget.
- Bind it in `bindCompetitiveSeat` and write it back in
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`).
- Since `players` are serialised wholesale
  (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts:103`), the per-seat field round-trips
  automatically; add a defensive load-time backfill for legacy saves missing
  the field (mirroring the seat-config / seat-colour backfills).
- Leave single-player paths unchanged; keep `state.maxHandSize` as the shared
  working field bound per seat.

## Constraints

- Keep `state.maxHandSize` as the shared working field; do not restructure the
  binding model.
- Do not change card-data `handSlotsAdded` values.
- Saves must remain backward compatible (legacy saves load unchanged).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sibling test child (tests are authored first, TDD).

## Deliverables

- Per-seat hand capacity bound, restored, and persisted; regression tests from
  the sibling child green; full suite green.

**Key Files:**

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add `maxHandSize` to `PlayerRecord`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — initialise the per-seat field in `createCompetitiveState`.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — bind/restore the per-seat hand capacity.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise/backfill the per-seat value.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — confirm `purchaseStaffCard` targets the bound (acting-seat) capacity.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — confirm `layoffStaffCard` targets the bound capacity.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-*.test.ts` — regression coverage.

# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.
- Automated find-related report appended below (if produced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — external chart library vs Phaser canvas.** Chart.js needs a canvas
  context; overlaying it on the Phaser canvas and keeping it out of
  headless/replay runs needs care. *Mitigation:* isolate the library behind
  `MainStreetStatsChart.ts`, lazy-load/skip in replay/headless, verify bundle
  size.
- **Risk — deferred vs legacy capture paths** could double-record or miss the
  final turn. *Mitigation:* record keyed by `turn` in the shared closing tail,
  with targeted unit tests for both paths.
- **Risk — save/load compatibility.** *Mitigation:* legacy fallback to `[]`,
  with a round-trip + legacy test.
- **Risk — three-column overflow at 1280×720.** *Mitigation:* recompute panel
  width/height and add a browser fit assertion.
- **Assumption — competitive-mode series scope.** In single-player the five
  series describe the run's economy. In competitive mode the shared
  `resourceBank` is seat-scoped during a turn; this brief assumes the graphs
  show the **human seat's** trajectory. *Open question, recorded in the
  Appendix* — the producer may instead want every seat as a separate series.
- **Assumption — "link to a more detailed screen" is satisfied by the third
  column**, per producer Q5; no separate scene is added.
- **Scope-creep risk:** additional stats or chart types beyond the five listed
  (producer Q4 = none) must be raised as separate work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Correct project?** This item was created in ContextHub (the Worklog
  CLI tool) but describes a Main Street game screen.
  - **Answer (producer): `tce-main-street`.** Source: interactive reply,
    2026-10-16. *Action:* item relocated — created as MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV in
    `tce-main-street`; the mis-filed WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02 was closed as a
    relocated duplicate.

- **Q2 — Per-turn history tracking.** The save holds only the current-turn
  `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score` snapshot; a full per-turn history must be added
  unless the save already carries one.
  - (A) Add per-turn history tracking, reusing the snapshot mechanism.
    **Recommended.**
  - (B) Use only static current values (no historical graphs).
  - **Answer (producer):** "Doesn't the save game have that snapshot? If not A
    otherwise reuse that mechanism." *Research:* inspected
    `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — the save persists only the **current**
    `weekStart*` snapshot, not a per-turn series; the `EconomyLedger` history
    is per-mutation and not serialised. Therefore **Option A** applies, reusing
    the `weekStart*` snapshot pattern and persisting a new series. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q3 — Chart/graph approach.**
  - (A) Phaser-based line/bar charts (custom `Graphics`). **Recommended** at
    the time of asking (no new dependency).
  - (B) External charting library (e.g. Chart.js).
  - (C) SVG line plots rendered as Phaser textures.
  - **Answer (producer): B** — use an external charting library (overrode the
    recommendation). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q4 — Additional stats?** Beyond profit/turn, businesses, cash, staff and
  reputation at end of turn.
  - **Answer (producer): No.** Only the five listed stats. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q5 — Summary-screen placement / detailed screen.** "Place the cash at end
  of turn on the summary screen and add a link to a more detailed screen" — is
  the Summary column the right place, with a button to a full-page graph view?
  - **Answer (producer): Add a third column.** The detailed graphs live in a
    third column of the Game Over overlay rather than a separate screen.
    Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope).** In competitive mode,
  should the graphs plot (i) only the human seat's trajectory, or (ii) every
  seat as a separate series? *Working assumption: (i) human seat only.* Noted
  for producer confirmation during review; not blocking.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** – Game-mode selector UI (completed)

### Repository file matches
